authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from a measured run and checked against the numbered source: `mk` defined on 15, `two_args` on 19, `pkg` on 24 calling on 25, the bare foreach/eval expression on 28, `combined` on 31 calling on 32. The call at line 28 is sourced from the MODULE, not from a rule, because there is no enclosing rule — that is the whole point of the fixture and the source is asserted explicitly rather than left as a wildcard.
rationale: `$(call NAME)` is a call, and a bare top-level expression is still a place references live. Two separate defects are pinned. (1) A macro must be a FUNCTION: a `$(call mk)` that resolves to a `constant` is a callee that cannot be called. (2) References used to be collected only beneath a `variable_assignment` and a `rule`, so a bare top-level expression — a `function_call` DIRECTLY under `makefile` — contributed nothing at all. That is not a corner case: `$(foreach t,… $(eval $(call mk,$(t))))` is the idiom nomad/GNUmakefile uses to reify its package targets, the corpus has one such site, and it produced ZERO edges before the fix. Positional parameters `$(1)`/`$(2)` are not declarations and must not become symbols.
